overview: High school teachers teach one or more subjects, such as math, English, science or history, to students in grades 9 to 12. They plan lessons, lecture and lead discussions, grade work, manage behavior and help students prepare for college and jobs. O*NET rates their social interest at a maximum 7.00 and knowledge of education and training at 4.69 out of 5. Public schools require a bachelor's degree, held by 77% in O*NET data, and a state teaching license. The BLS May 2025 median is $72,040 across 1,065,210 jobs, one of the largest careers in the country.
pay: High school teachers earn a median of $72,040, and the top 10% earn $107,600 or more. Washington, California and New York have the highest state medians, from $97,070 to $102,670. Texas has the most jobs, 111,660, at a median of $63,590. Oklahoma has the lowest state median, $48,710.

faq.q: How much do high school teachers make?
faq.a: The BLS May 2025 median is $72,040 a year. The middle half earn between $59,980 and $92,570. Washington ($102,670) and California ($101,370) pay the most, while Mississippi ($50,980) and Oklahoma ($48,710) have the lowest state medians. Districts usually pay more for a master's degree.

faq.q: What degree do you need to teach high school?
faq.a: You need a bachelor's degree, which 77% of high school teachers hold in O*NET data, plus a state teaching license. Many major in the subject they teach and complete a teacher preparation program. There are 12 related majors, including secondary education and teaching.

faq.q: What skills do high school teachers need?
faq.a: O*NET rates reading comprehension, active listening, learning strategies and speaking at 4 out of 5 for this job. Self-control stands out as a work style, since you manage classes of teenagers every day. Knowledge of computers is rated 3.58.

faq.q: What can high school teachers do instead?
faq.a: The closest moves are adult education and ESL instructors (92% match), postsecondary English teachers (81%) and Instructional Coordinators (81%), based on O*NET 31.0. English professors earn $78,760, 9% more, according to BLS May 2025 data, but usually need a graduate degree.
